text: And its status as the means to the ultimate liberation has been recognized. For the Shruti states, "Through the attainment of spiritual yoga, having realized the Divine, the wise person transcends joy and sorrow" (Katha 2.12), and the Smriti also says, "When the intellect becomes unwavering in Samadhi, then you shall attain Yoga" (Gita 2.53). Therefore, the sequence starting with the disciple's inquiry, austerities, service, and the use of rejuvenatives has been set aside. Regarding the statement "Now, therefore, the inquiry into Brahman" (Brahma Sutra 1.1.1), Shankaracharya has clearly established that the meaning of the word "atha" (now) does not denote the lack of qualification for the inquiry into Brahman, but rather indicates the sequence of calmness (śama), self-control (dama), and other qualities as prescribed by the relevant texts, for the purpose of dedicating the seeker who is distinguished by the possession of the fourfold qualifications.
